newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - Copper spreads to dominate.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - Copper spreads to dominate.

text.p: Rampant nearby backwardations will continue to transfix the London Metal Exchange (LME) copper market this week as tight dates are worked through and February options are declared, traders said.

The cash/three months backwardation was at a high $235 on Friday evening, while the cash/one day premium was at $23, with the market still working through the period of extreme tightness that ranges through until the middle of this month.
"Cash for a day and the TOM (tomorrow/next day) are likely to remain well bid for a while," one trader said.

Other metals were expected to resume the strong bounces seen on Friday after mid-week wobbles as a wave of buying interest spurred on zinc and nickel in particular. Zinc reached its highest for two years.
"The sell-offs all appear to have run their course...and there has been good buying seen (in zinc)," said William Adams, analyst at LME trader Rudolf Wolff and Co.
In copper, the overall backwardation had narrowed considerably from the peaks of $335 reached early last week - a reflection of the tight nearby prompts falling out of the system.

However, the spread remained high, and the shorts, believed to number a major Far Eastern trade house, faced little respite. This was because the long-holder - a European merchant - was looking to take delivery for physical needs, other traders said.

One requirement was said to be for Singapore metal, so last Friday's bumper 26,100-tonne stock increase in LME inventories, which resulted in metal being delivered to a wide spread of locations, suited the purpose.
"They are doing a bit of warrant sifting at the moment," one trader said.

On Friday, 4,525 tonnes were delivered into Singapore, taking the total for this location to 45,000 tonnes. Overall LME inventories were at 191,750 tonnes, 101,700 tonnes above last November's low-point and the highest since October 1995.
The copper market would also focus on options this week -- initially today, when the LME introduces traded average price options (TAPOS) for both copper mand aluminium, which are cash settled.
On Wednesday February regular traded options will be declared, with copper strikes again keenly watched.
Elsewhere, traders would be looking for aluminium to convincingly regain the $1,625 a tonne level, having ended last week at $1,624.
